hypothesis: A structured AI risk dashboard that aggregates a concise set of AI-specific leading and lagging indicators (including drift, fairness, robustness, explainability, and cross-model concentration metrics) will (a) detect emerging AI stress earlier and (b) support more consistent, board-relevant escalation decisions than a traditional KPI/KRI pack that lacks AI-specific and portfolio-level metrics.

baseline.description: Traditional KPI/KRI monitoring pack for AI-enabled processes that focuses on business outcomes and generic operational indicators, but lacks explicit AI model health, fairness, robustness, explainability, or portfolio concentration metrics.

characteristics: No explicit model-level metrics (no drift, data quality, calibration, robustness, or fairness indicators).
No explicit leading indicators of AI instability; focus is on realized performance and incidents.
No portfolio-level aggregation across multiple AI models (no concentration or correlation view).
No formal thresholds tied to AI-specific escalation paths.

baseline.user_journey: Risk and business teams review the traditional KPI/KRI pack weekly and simulate how they would brief a board committee on AI-related risk using only those metrics to identify emerging issues in sample scenarios.

treatment.description: AI-specific risk dashboard and heatmap that translates model health into business-relevant, board-level indicators, combines leading and lagging metrics, and aggregates risk across a portfolio of models with thresholds and escalation triggers.
treatment.user_journey: Using the same synthetic AI portfolio and scenarios as the baseline, risk and business users interact with the AI risk dashboard generated by the experiment, then simulate their board briefing and escalation decisions based on the richer AI-specific metrics and heatmaps.

workloads.name: workload_1_synthetic_portfolio_generation
workloads.description: Generate a synthetic portfolio of AI models and associated business data streams representing a universal bank with multiple AI-enabled use cases.
steps: Define 8–12 synthetic AI models across business lines (e.g., retail_credit_scoring, SME_credit_scoring, market_making_agent, AML_transaction_monitoring, card_fraud_detection, marketing_next_best_action, LLM_customer_service_assistant, algo_execution_router).
For each model, define: business_line, product_type, model_type (e.g., gradient_boosting, deep_neural_net, RL_policy, LLM), criticality_tier (1–3), auto_decision_share_pct (0–100%).

Simulate 12–24 months of monthly or weekly data per model, including: volume_of_decisions, approval_rates, realized_outcomes (e.g., defaults, frauds, PnL), incident_counts, complaint_rates, override_rates_by_humans.

Generate underlying feature distributions and model outputs, including at least: 2–3 key numeric input features per model; model_score_distributions; protected_attributes or proxies for fairness analysis (e.g., gender, age_band, geography) with synthetic labels and decisions.

Introduce controlled structural patterns for later evaluation: correlated_shocks_across_models (e.g., macro_regime_shift at time T0); increased_data_drift on specified models after T0; fairness_deterioration for certain segments; growing_auto_decision_share for selected high-criticality models; latent_correlations among model_outputs to enable concentration/correlation analysis.

workloads.name: workload_2_metric_computation_engine
workloads.description: Compute baseline business KPIs and AI-specific risk metrics on the synthetic portfolio over time.
steps: Implement baseline KPI/KRI computation for each model and period: approval_rate, default_rate_or_loss_rate, fraud_detected_rate (where applicable), PnL_contribution, complaint_rate_per_10k_customers, incident_count_by_severity, system_uptime_pct (synthetic).
Implement AI-specific metric computation for each model and period:
- Drift metrics: distribution_based_drift_score for inputs and outputs using e.g., population_stability_index or Jensen-Shannon_divergence, normalized to [0,1].

- Stability metrics: stability_index based on change in model_coefficients or prediction patterns between periods (for black-box models, use change in feature_importance rankings or prediction_rank_correlation).
- Robustness metrics: robustness_score from performance under synthetic perturbations (e.g., noise_injection, feature_dropout) on a held-out sample.
- Fairness metrics: group_fairness_gap measures (e.g., difference_in_approval_rates or TPR/FPR between advantaged and disadvantaged groups) and fairness_gap_flags above governance thresholds.
- Explainability metrics: explainability_coverage_pct (share of predictions with available local explanations) and complexity_proxy (e.g., average_shap_importance_entropy).
- Autonomy metrics: auto_decision_share_pct; human_override_rate (fraction of AI decisions changed by humans); escalation_rate_to_humans.
- Correlation metrics: rolling_pairwise_correlation_of_model_outputs for logically related model pairs.
- Surprise metrics (for LLMs or RL agents): surprise_index derived from rate_of_novel_action_patterns, high-variance_outputs, or disagreement_with_reference_policy.

Aggregate metrics to portfolio-level each period: number_of_models_above_threshold per metric; concentration_measures (e.g., Herfindahl-Hirschman index) for exposure_by_model, vendor_dependency, feature_family_dependency; average_cross_model_output_correlation for defined clusters of models.

workloads.name: workload_3_dashboard_and_heatmap_generation
workloads.description: Render both baseline and treatment dashboards and risk heatmaps from the computed metrics.
steps: For the baseline condition, generate a static dashboard (e.g., in a Jupyter notebook or simple web front-end) showing per-model and aggregate business KPIs and KRIs without any AI-specific risk measures.
For the treatment condition, generate additional visualizations:
- Per-model health cards summarizing: drift_scores, fairness_gap, robustness_score, stability_index, explainability_coverage_pct, auto_decision_share_pct, recent_incident_count, and risk_tier.

- A matrix-style AI risk heatmap with models on one axis and key AI risk dimensions (drift, fairness, robustness, explainability, autonomy_level, correlation) on the other; cells color-coded by normalized risk level.
- A portfolio concentration and correlation heatmap capturing exposure_concentration and pairwise_output_correlation.
- Time-series plots of leading indicators (e.g., drift_scores, fairness_gaps, stability_index) alongside lagging indicators (e.g., default_rates, incidents, complaints).
- Governance overlay views highlighting where thresholds have been crossed and what trigger level (e.g., yellow/amber/red) is currently active.
Allow the user to select time windows (e.g., pre-shock vs post-shock periods) and dynamically inspect both baseline and treatment dashboards for those periods.

workloads.name: workload_4_thresholds_triggers_and_escalation_rules
workloads.description: Define and apply governance thresholds and escalation rules tied to AI risk metrics for the treatment condition.
steps: Define configurable thresholds for each AI-specific metric, using governance-style bands instead of arbitrary statistical cutoffs, for example:
- drift_score: green < 0.2, amber 0.2–0.4, red > 0.4.
- fairness_gap (absolute difference in approval_rate between groups): green < 3pp, amber 3–5pp, red > 5pp.
- robustness_score: green >= 0.9, amber 0.8–0.9, red < 0.8.
- explainability_coverage_pct: green >= 90%, amber 70–90%, red < 70%.
- auto_decision_share_pct for Tier 1 models: green <= 50%, amber 50–80%, red > 80% unless explicitly approved.
- cross_model_output_correlation: green if |rho| <= 0.5, amber 0.5–0.8, red > 0.8 for models within same risk channel.
Define rule-based triggers that map metric bands into actions, for example:
- Single red threshold on drift_score or fairness_gap for any Tier 1 model => heightened_monitoring + mandatory_management_review within X days.
- Two consecutive amber periods on stability_index plus rising default_rate => model_change_freeze and technical_review.
- Red concentration_index and high cross_model_correlation in the same risk channel => require portfolio-level diversification_plan and board_notification.

Implement a simple rules engine that, for each period and model, evaluates metrics against thresholds and records triggered_actions, including simulated severity_level, required_approver_role, and expected_completion_time.
Produce an escalation_log data structure that can be visualized and compared to realized incidents and business losses in synthetic scenarios.

workloads.name: workload_5_scenario_replay_and_comparative_evaluation
workloads.description: Replay defined stress scenarios across both baseline and treatment dashboards to quantify detection lead time and consistency of escalation recommendations.
steps: Define at least three synthetic scenarios embedded in the data:
- Scenario_A_gradual_drift: slow, monotonic distribution shift in key input features and predictions for a high-criticality credit model, leading to a rising default rate after a lag.
- Scenario_B_fairness_shift: change in application mix leading to increased unfair treatment of a protected group, with complaints rising only after several periods.

- Scenario_C_correlation_spike: multiple trading or market-facing models begin to respond similarly to the same signals, increasing output correlations and concentration of exposures before any realized loss event.

For each scenario, mark the ground_truth_time_of_structural_change (first period where underlying risk starts to increase) and the ground_truth_time_of_realized_loss_or_incident (first period with noticeable default/PnL/incident impact).

For the baseline condition, define detection_time_baseline as the earliest period when a predefined rule based solely on KPIs/KRIs would reasonably flag emerging risk (e.g., default_rate above band, PnL_volatility increase, complaint_rate spike).
For the treatment condition, define detection_time_treatment as the earliest period when AI-specific metrics plus governance thresholds trigger a non-trivial escalation_rule (e.g., amber/red status).
Compute lead_time_gain = detection_time_baseline - detection_time_treatment (positive values indicate earlier detection by the treatment).

Assess escalation_consistency by simulating multiple synthetic committees/users: programmatically vary risk appetite or noise in decision thresholds and see how often the same escalation outcome is chosen under baseline vs treatment given the same underlying data.
Collect all outputs (lead_times, escalation_decisions, trigger_histories) into a structured evaluation dataset for later analysis and visualization.

data_controls: Use the same synthetic dataset (same random seeds and scenario configurations) for both baseline and treatment conditions.
Ensure that any noise or randomness in metric computation (e.g., subsampling) is either controlled via fixed seeds or clearly recorded in metadata.
Verify that scenario_onset_times and underlying structural changes are identical across baseline and treatment.
model_controls: Keep model structures and parameters fixed across runs; experiments vary only in which metrics are surfaced and how they are aggregated, not in the underlying model behavior.
If surrogate models or explanation tools are used (e.g., SHAP, LIME), keep their configuration constant across runs.
presentation_controls: Ensure that baseline and treatment dashboards are presented with comparable visual quality (e.g., similar color schemes, resolution, and layout discipline) so that differences in outcomes are attributable to metric content rather than interface design.
Limit the number of panels per screen in both conditions to avoid bias from information overload in one condition only.
evaluation_controls: When collecting human-annotated judgements (optional extension), randomize whether a given evaluator sees the baseline or treatment dashboard first to mitigate order effects.
Use a pre-specified set of detection and escalation rules for both conditions to avoid post-hoc tuning in favor of the treatment.

metrics.name: detection_lead_time_gain
metrics.description: For each scenario and model, the difference in periods between baseline and treatment in detecting emerging AI risk (positive means treatment detects earlier).

metrics.name: early_warning_sensitivity
metrics.description: Fraction of scenarios where the treatment condition flags a non-trivial trigger before realized loss/incident time.

metrics.name: false_positive_trigger_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of time periods with red or amber triggers under the treatment condition that are not followed by any realized incident or material loss within a specified forecast window.

metrics.name: escalation_decision_consistency
metrics.description: Across simulated or human evaluation runs, the proportion of times the same escalation decision (e.g., monitor, management_review, partial_shutdown) is taken for the same underlying model-period.

metrics.name: portfolio_risk_signal_sharpness
metrics.description: Normalized contrast between high-risk and low-risk models in the portfolio heatmap, e.g., using between-model variance of composite risk scores.

metrics.name: metric_computation_cost
metrics.description: Compute/resources required to generate all AI-specific metrics and dashboards for one full portfolio run.

metrics.name: governance_alignment_index
metrics.description: Optional: composite score mapping how well the triggered actions align with pre-defined governance objectives (e.g., avoid late response, avoid unnecessary shutdowns).

primary: Mean detection_lead_time_gain across all defined scenarios is strictly greater than 0 and at least 1 full time_period for Tier_1 models.
early_warning_sensitivity under the treatment condition is >= 0.8 (i.e., at least 80% of embedded scenarios are flagged before realized incident/loss).
secondary: false_positive_trigger_rate under the treatment condition remains <= 0.3, indicating that increased sensitivity does not come at the cost of unmanageable noise.
escalation_decision_consistency under treatment is at least 10 percentage points higher than under baseline when evaluated with the same set of decision rules or human raters.

portfolio_risk_signal_sharpness under treatment exceeds a pre-defined threshold (e.g., normalized_variance_of_risk_scores >= 0.5), indicating clear differentiation of higher-risk models for board focus.
interpretation_notes: If the treatment improves lead time but produces an unacceptably high false_positive_trigger_rate, further work is required to tune thresholds and aggregation logic before recommending board-level adoption.

If treatment fails to improve detection_lead_time_gain for certain failure modes (e.g., fairness_shift, correlation_spike), this highlights gaps in the chosen metrics suite and should inform chapter guidance about limitations and future enhancements.

failure_modes.name: metric_instability_or_noise
failure_modes.description: AI-specific metrics (e.g., drift, fairness) fluctuate excessively due to low sample sizes or noisy synthetic data, leading to unreliable triggers.
mitigations: Implement minimum_support_constraints (e.g., require N>=100 observations per group) before computing fairness metrics.
Smooth time-series metrics using moving_averages or exponential_smoothing and compare raw vs smoothed values.
Log confidence_intervals or uncertainty_measures alongside point estimates.

failure_modes.name: miscalibrated_thresholds
failure_modes.description: Thresholds for amber/red bands are chosen arbitrarily, causing too many or too few alerts and distorting evaluation of the treatment.
mitigations: Pre-define thresholds based on regulatory or industry heuristics (e.g., common PSI thresholds, fairness gaps) rather than tuning to experimental results.
Run sensitivity_analyses across a grid of threshold combinations and report how success metrics change.
Document all threshold choices in configuration files stored with the experiment.

failure_modes.name: overly_simple_scenarios
failure_modes.description: Synthetic scenarios are too stylized, making it trivial for any metric set (baseline or treatment) to detect issues, thereby underestimating the benefit of AI-specific metrics.
mitigations: Include both gradual and abrupt regime shifts and overlapping signals across models.
Ensure at least some scenarios where business KPIs move only after a lag, while AI-specific metrics move earlier.
Document scenario_design_parameters and allow extension with more complex cases.

failure_modes.name: implementation_bias_in_dashboard_design
failure_modes.description: Differences in layout, colors, or clarity of the treatment dashboard (vs baseline) inadvertently drive perceived improvements independent of metric content.
mitigations: Use a shared visual design system (same fonts, color palette, chart types) for both dashboards.
If conducting human studies, randomize color mappings and layout where possible while keeping content constant.
Provide raw metric tables in addition to visualizations for algorithmic evaluation.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_synthetic_data
failure_modes.description: Metric choices and thresholds inadvertently exploit peculiarities of the synthetic dataset that would not generalize to real institutions.
mitigations: Use multiple, distinct synthetic portfolios with different parameterizations to test robustness of findings.
Where feasible, allow institutions to rerun the experiment on their own de-identified data.
Emphasize in documentation that this is a reference design, not a calibrated production rulebook.

hardware.cpu: Modern multi-core CPU; no GPU required.

run_instructions: Create and activate a virtual environment (example with venv): `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` (Linux/macOS) or `.venv\Scripts\activate` (Windows).
Install dependencies: `pip install -r requirements.txt`. The requirements file should list the libraries specified in required_environment.
Generate synthetic data: run `python src/generate_synthetic_portfolio.py --config config/portfolio_config.yaml --out data_synthetic/portfolio.parquet`.
Compute metrics: run `python src/compute_metrics.py --config config/metrics_config.yaml --input data_synthetic/portfolio.parquet --out data_synthetic/metrics.parquet`.
- Option A (static reports): run `python src/render_dashboards.py --metrics data_synthetic/metrics.parquet --out reports/` to produce HTML/PNG summaries for both baseline and treatment conditions.
- Option B (interactive notebooks): launch `jupyter lab` and open `notebooks/ch6_dashboard_comparison.ipynb` to interactively explore baseline vs treatment dashboards, heatmaps, and trigger logs.
Run threshold and trigger simulation: `python src/run_triggers_and_scenarios.py --metrics data_synthetic/metrics.parquet --config config/triggers_config.yaml --out data_synthetic/triggers.parquet`.

Evaluate experiment outcomes: open `notebooks/ch6_experiment_evaluation.ipynb` to compute detection_lead_time_gain, early_warning_sensitivity, false_positive_trigger_rate, escalation_decision_consistency, and portfolio_risk_signal_sharpness. All results should be stored in `evidence/` as JSON/CSV files conforming to the evidence_schema.

Optional (institutional replay): adapt `config/portfolio_config.yaml` and point `compute_metrics.py` to an institution-specific, de-identified dataset following the expected schema to rerun the experiment on real data.

run_id.description: Unique identifier for this run (e.g., UUID4).

data_seed.description: Random seed used for synthetic data generation.

config_files.description: List of config files used (portfolio, metrics, triggers).

scenario_results.description: Per-scenario comparison of baseline vs treatment.

per_model_time_series.description: Optional but recommended: per-model, per-period metrics for reproducibility and deeper analysis.
